- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly to capture upside momentum.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor (e.g., 0.85) to subsequent forecasts.
- In 30-day horizon, model shows persistent lag in capturing upward trends; add 1-2% buffer to forecast if sentiment is bullish and price has been trending up.
- If sentiment shifts from neutral to bullish within 5 days, model often fails to adjust; force a 1-3 day lagged correction to match sentiment momentum.
- Model underestimates true price volatility in high-sentiment periods; increase forecast standard deviation by 10-15% if sentiment > 0.7 for 3+ consecutive days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong upward momentum, model tends to underestimate final peak; add 2-5% upward adjustment to final 5-7 days.
